accommodation.name: St Christopher's Inn Paris - Canal
accommodation.notes: Hostel: St Christopher's Inn Paris - Canal (159 rue de Crimée, 75019 Paris). 12-Bed Mixed Dormitory. Total: €119.59 (Paid online: €21.52, Balance at property: €108.47 including €10.40 taxes). Social hostel near Canal de l'Ourcq. Metro: Crimée (Line 7) or Laumière (Line 5).

arrival.notes: Flight arrives 10:35 at Orly. Take Orlybus to Denfert-Rochereau (€9.50, ~30 min), then Metro Line 4 to Gare du Nord, transfer to Line 5 to Laumière (~40 min metro). OR: RER B to Gare du Nord + walk. Total transit: 60-75 min. Estimated hostel arrival: 11:45-12:30.

departure.notes: Eurostar direct train to London St Pancras Int'l (Coach 4 - Seat 93). Departure at 07:32, arrives 09:00 (2h 28m). REMINDER: Complete Passenger Information (API) online and ensure you have your UK Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) before travel.

days.title: Arrival Day - Latin Quarter, Montmartre Sunset & Le Marais

timeBlocks.name: morning
timeBlocks.description: Flight arrival from Barcelona. Transport to hostel, check-in/luggage storage. Purchase 2-Day Museum Pass online or at FNAC/tourism office.

activities.name: Airport Arrival & Transport to Hostel
activities.notes: Take Orlybus to Denfert-Rochereau (€9.50), then metro to the hostel. Total: 60-75 min.

activities.name: St Christopher's Inn Check-in / Luggage Storage
activities.notes: Store luggage if room not ready. Freshen up and prepare for afternoon exploration. Social hostel with bar - great for meeting people later.

activities.name: Purchase 2-Day Museum Pass
activities.timeRestriction: Available online or at FNAC stores, tourism offices
activities.notes: CRITICAL: Buy 2-Day Pass (€55) for Days 2 & 3. Activate Saturday morning at first museum. Saves €30 vs 4-day pass. Can buy online now or at FNAC/tourism office in Latin Quarter.

bookingDetails.advanceTimeNeeded: Can buy same-day or in advance online

timeBlocks.name: lunch
timeBlocks.description: Latin Quarter lunch - student-friendly bistros and cafés around Panthéon/Sorbonne area

activities.name: Latin Quarter Lunch
activities.notes: Student-friendly bistros near Sorbonne. Try Rue Mouffetard for casual options. Budget €10-15 for lunch.

timeBlocks.name: afternoon
timeBlocks.description: Latin Quarter literary exploration - Shakespeare and Company, medieval streets, Panthéon exterior, Luxembourg Gardens. Light arrival day activities.

activities.name: Shakespeare and Company
activities.notes: Iconic English-language bookstore on the Left Bank. Literary pilgrimage spot. Free to browse, cozy atmosphere.

activities.name: Rue Saint-Julien-le-Pauvre & Rue Galande
activities.notes: Medieval streets near Shakespeare & Co. Picturesque narrow lanes with old architecture.

activities.name: Panthéon (Exterior)
activities.notes: Neoclassical mausoleum in Latin Quarter. View exterior today, save interior visit (€11.50 student) for Day 4.

activities.name: Rue Mouffetard & Place de la Contrescarpe
activities.timeRestriction: Market best in mornings, but shops open until evening
activities.notes: Historic market street dating to Roman times. Cafés, food shops, local atmosphere. One of oldest streets in Paris.

activities.name: Jardin du Luxembourg
activities.timeRestriction: Open dawn to dusk (~08:00-21:00 in Oct)
activities.notes: Beautiful formal gardens with palace, fountains, sculptures. Relax before evening activities. Popular with students and locals.

timeBlocks.name: evening_part1
timeBlocks.description: Montmartre evening - Sacré-Cœur sunset, artists' square, picturesque streets. 15 min metro from Latin Quarter (Line 4 to Abbesses).

activities.name: Metro to Montmartre
activities.notes: Metro to Abbesses station (~15 min) - beautiful Art Nouveau entrance (designed by Hector Guimard).

activities.name: Rue des Abbesses
activities.notes: Charming Montmartre street. Note the Art Nouveau metro entrance (designed by Hector Guimard). Local cafés and shops.

activities.name: Villa Léandre
activities.notes: Hidden cobblestone alley with English-style cottages. Secret gem of Montmartre. Very Instagrammable.

activities.name: Place Dalida
activities.notes: Bust of French singer Dalida with nice viewpoint over Paris. Locals touch the bust for good luck.

activities.name: Rue de l'Abreuvoir
activities.notes: One of the most picturesque streets in Paris. Classic Montmartre view with Sacré-Cœur in background. Featured in many paintings.

activities.name: Basilique du Sacré-Cœur
activities.notes: White Romano-Byzantine basilica atop Montmartre hill. FREE entry to basilica. CATCH SUNSET from steps (around 19:30-20:00 in Oct). Panoramic Paris views. Dome costs extra (€6) if you want to climb - closes at 20:00 so skip today. PERSONAL RATING: 10/10 - excellent place to visit, always street musicians playing and a beautiful atmosphere.

activities.name: Place du Tertre
activities.notes: Historic artists' square behind Sacré-Cœur. Street artists doing portraits and caricatures. Touristy but iconic Montmartre experience. More atmospheric in evening than midday crowds.
activities.cost: free (portraits cost €20-50 if you want one)

timeBlocks.name: evening_part2
timeBlocks.description: Le Marais evening - L'As du Fallafel dinner, Place des Vosges, thrift shopping on Rue de la Verrerie. Metro from Montmartre to Le Marais (~20 min).

activities.name: Metro Montmartre to Le Marais
activities.notes: Metro to Saint-Paul (~20 min), or walk down from Montmartre if you have energy.

activities.name: L'As du Fallafel
activities.timeRestriction: CLOSED Friday evening & all day Saturday. Open Sun-Thu 11:00-23:00
activities.notes: Famous falafel spot in Jewish quarter (Rue des Rosiers). Budget €8-12 for falafel sandwich. Lines can be long but move fast. Lenny Kravitz's favorite spot! CONFIRM it's Friday (open today!).

activities.name: Rue de la Verrerie (Thrift Stores)
activities.timeRestriction: Kilo Shop open until 21:00 Mon-Sat (might be closed), Free'P'Star open until 20:00
activities.notes: Vintage/thrift stores: Kilo Shop (pay by weight), Free'P'Star. Might be closed by now but street is charming to walk. Save detailed shopping for another day if stores closed.

activities.name: Place des Vosges
activities.timeRestriction: Park closed at night, but square is accessible 24/7
activities.notes: Oldest planned square in Paris (1612). Beautiful arcaded square with red brick buildings. Atmospheric at night. Victor Hugo lived at #6.

alternatives.name: Musée de Cluny (Medieval Museum)
alternatives.reason_not_selected: €9 student, 90 min visit. Too much for arrival day. Can add if you skip some Latin Quarter walking or save for Day 4.
alternatives.when_to_add: Day 4 if you want more museums

alternatives.name: Saint-Étienne-du-Mont Church
alternatives.reason_not_selected: Near Panthéon, free, 30 min. Can add if you have extra time in Latin Quarter.
alternatives.when_to_add: Add to afternoon if desired, near Panthéon

alternatives.name: Notre-Dame Exterior Walk-by
alternatives.reason_not_selected: Quick 15 min stop from Shakespeare & Co. Saved for Day 4 when doing full Île de la Cité tour.
alternatives.when_to_add: Afternoon if near area, or save for Day 4

alternatives.name: Île de la Cité Walk
alternatives.reason_not_selected: Saved for Day 4 comprehensive islands visit with Sainte-Chapelle interior.
alternatives.when_to_add: Day 4 afternoon

alternatives.name: Saint-Germain-des-Prés (Literary Cafés)
alternatives.reason_not_selected: Near Luxembourg Gardens. Can add if time, or save for another evening if time allows.
alternatives.when_to_add: After Luxembourg if time, or another evening

alternatives.name: Maison de Victor Hugo
alternatives.reason_not_selected: Free museum at Place des Vosges. Opens 10:00-18:00 (closed by evening). Can add to Day 4.
alternatives.when_to_add: Day 4 Le Marais daytime visit

alternatives.name: Canal Saint-Martin Walk
alternatives.reason_not_selected: 5 min from hostel. Can do as evening/night activity or before sleep. Not scheduled to keep flexibility.
alternatives.when_to_add: Any evening, especially if back at hostel early

research_notes.notes: Day 1 restructured to include Montmartre sunset (better than rushing at 4am Day 5) and Le Marais evening (moved from Day 4 to free up time for Palais Garnier). Light activities appropriate for arrival day. All free except transport and dinner. Bike not recommended due to luggage and evening activities across different areas.

days.title: Museum Pass Day 1 - Royal Paris & Arc de Triomphe

timeBlocks.name: morning
timeBlocks.description: ACTIVATE Museum Pass today! Tuileries Gardens, Place de la Concorde, Pont Alexandre III, then Hôtel de la Marine - CONFIRMED timed entry 11:00. Bike recommended.

activities.name: Bike Rental (Vélib')
activities.notes: Pick up Vélib' bike near hostel. 7-day pass (€8) or pay-as-you-go. E-bikes recommended for longer distances. Stations at all major attractions.

activities.name: Bike/Metro to Tuileries
activities.notes: Bike ride: 25 min. Or metro (~25 min). Biking recommended for beautiful route along Seine.
activities.cost: €2.15 metro OR included in bike pass

activities.name: Jardin des Tuileries
activities.notes: Historic formal gardens between Louvre and Place de la Concorde. Morning stroll, sculptures, fountains. Part of old royal palace grounds.

activities.name: Place de la Concorde
activities.notes: Largest square in Paris. Egyptian obelisk (3,300 years old!). Site of Louis XVI and Marie Antoinette executions during French Revolution. Views of Champs-Élysées, Eiffel Tower, Madeleine Church.

activities.name: Pont Alexandre III
activities.notes: Most ornate bridge in Paris. Art Nouveau lamps, gold statues, views of Eiffel Tower and Invalides. Built for 1900 World's Fair. Very Instagrammable! Quick round-trip detour from Concorde while waiting for the Hôtel de la Marine time slot.

activities.name: Hôtel de la Marine
activities.notes: ✅ CONFIRMED - ticket #101385120876601, timed entry 18/10/2026 at 11:00, free with Museum Pass (ACTIVATE PASS HERE - Day 1 of 2-day pass). Stunning 18th-century palace on Place de la Concorde. Opulent apartments (Appartement des Intendants), Crown Jewels storage history. 2-hour visit. Metro Line 1 - Concorde stop.

timeBlocks.name: lunch
timeBlocks.description: Rue Cler market street lunch, or bistro near Invalides/Eiffel area.

activities.name: Rue Cler Market Street Lunch
activities.timeRestriction: Market best morning-early afternoon, cafés open longer
activities.notes: Charming pedestrian market street in 7th arrondissement. Food shops, bakeries, cafés. Pick up picnic supplies or sit at café. Budget €12-20 for lunch.

timeBlocks.name: afternoon
timeBlocks.description: Les Invalides & Napoleon's Tomb (Museum Pass), then Champ de Mars for a relaxed view of the Eiffel Tower from below (tower visit itself now happens Day 4).

activities.name: Les Invalides & Musée de l'Armée
activities.notes: MUSEUM PASS INCLUDED. NO RESERVATION NEEDED - just walk in with the Museum Pass. Napoleon's Tomb under golden dome - incredible! Army museum with armor, weapons, WWI/WWII exhibits. 2 hours recommended. One of best museums in Paris.

activities.name: Champ de Mars
activities.notes: Large public greenspace at base of Eiffel Tower. Great for rest, photos looking up at the tower from below. Former military training ground. NOTE: going up the tower itself is saved for Day 4 (quick 1st floor visit).

timeBlocks.name: evening
timeBlocks.description: Trocadéro for the classic Eiffel Tower view and the sparkling light show at dusk, then Arc de Triomphe rooftop (Museum Pass) for 360° night views of Paris. Bike back or metro.

activities.name: Trocadéro
activities.timeRestriction: Best at sunset and for Eiffel Tower light show (on the hour after dark)
activities.notes: BEST Eiffel Tower view! Esplanade du Trocadéro across from tower. Wait for sparkling lights (every hour on the hour for 5 min after dark - starts ~20:00 in Oct). Iconic photo spot.

activities.name: Bike/Metro to Arc de Triomphe
activities.notes: Bike: 15 min uphill along Avenue Kléber. Or take metro Line 6 - board at Bir-Hakeim (right next to Champ de Mars/Eiffel Tower), ride straight through Trocadéro, continue to Charles de Gaulle-Étoile (Arc de Triomphe) - no transfer needed, ~15 min total.
activities.cost: €2.15 metro OR included in bike pass

activities.name: Arc de Triomphe (Rooftop)
activities.timeRestriction: Open 10:00-23:00 (Apr-Sep), 10:00-22:30 (Oct-Mar). Last entry 45 min before close.
activities.notes: MUSEUM PASS INCLUDED. 360° rooftop views of Paris at night - see Eiffel sparkling, Champs-Élysées, La Défense, Sacré-Cœur. 284 steps to top. Tomb of Unknown Soldier beneath. NO RESERVATION NEEDED - just walk in with the Museum Pass. PERSONAL RATING: 7/10 - good 360° city view but the top is caged/fenced in, which takes away from the experience a bit.

activities.name: Return to Hostel
activities.notes: Bike: 30 min ride back (or return bike and take metro, ~25-30 min).
activities.cost: €2.15 metro OR included in bike pass

alternatives.name: Musée de l'Orangerie (Monet's Water Lilies)
alternatives.reason_not_selected: Museum Pass included, 90 min visit in Tuileries Gardens. Would need to cut Hôtel de la Marine. Can swap if you prefer Impressionism over royal apartments.
alternatives.when_to_add: Morning instead of Hôtel de la Marine, or squeeze in before lunch

alternatives.name: Grand Palais
alternatives.reason_not_selected: Currently under renovation (exterior only). Check for temporary exhibitions.
alternatives.when_to_add: Walk-by only unless special exhibition

alternatives.name: Petit Palais
alternatives.reason_not_selected: FREE permanent collection (Belle Époque art), 90 min. Near Pont Alexandre III. Would need to cut lunch time or skip Champ de Mars rest.
alternatives.when_to_add: After Pont Alexandre III if you want more museums

alternatives.name: Champs-Élysées Walk
alternatives.reason_not_selected: From Arc de Triomphe downhill to Place de la Concorde (30 min). Touristy shopping street. Can walk after Arc if you have energy, but it's mostly chain stores.
alternatives.when_to_add: Evening after Arc de Triomphe, before returning to hostel

alternatives.name: Musée du Quai Branly (Non-European Art)
alternatives.reason_not_selected: Museum Pass included, 90 min, near Eiffel Tower. Would need to skip Les Invalides. Only if you prefer indigenous/African/Asian/Oceanic art over military history.
alternatives.when_to_add: Afternoon instead of Les Invalides

alternatives.name: Musée Rodin (Sculpture & Gardens)
alternatives.reason_not_selected: Museum Pass included, 90 min, between Invalides and Eiffel. Would need to cut other afternoon activities or skip Champ de Mars rest. Garden alone worth visiting.
alternatives.when_to_add: Afternoon if you skip Les Invalides or shorten Eiffel time

alternatives.name: Eiffel Tower visit
alternatives.reason_not_selected: Moved to Day 4 as a quick 1st-floor-only visit per user preference, rather than the full 2nd floor stairs experience on this already-packed Museum Pass day.
alternatives.when_to_add: See Day 4 early morning

research_notes.notes: Day 2 is Museum Pass Day 1 activation. Focused on royal/monumental Paris - gardens, palaces, Les Invalides. Eiffel Tower itself moved to Day 4 (quick 1st floor visit) - Champ de Mars and Trocadéro remain on Day 2 as free viewpoints of the tower from below/across the river. Arc de Triomphe at night for sparkling Eiffel views from above. Long day but bike helps. Hôtel de la Marine and Invalides both need timed bookings with Museum Pass. Budget total: €55 (Museum Pass) + €8 (bike optional) = €63 main costs.

days.title: Museum Pass Day 2 - Louvre, Sainte-Chapelle & Panthéon

timeBlocks.name: morning
timeBlocks.description: MUSEUM PASS DAY 2 (last day - must use today!). CONFIRMED Louvre timed entry at 11:00 - leave with buffer time.

activities.name: Metro to Louvre
activities.notes: Metro to the Louvre (~25 min). Leaving at 10:00 gives buffer before the confirmed 11:00 entry.

activities.name: Musée du Louvre (Morning Session)
activities.timeRestriction: CONFIRMED timed entry 11:00 on 19/10/2026. Open 09:00-18:00. Entrance via Carrousel, Pyramid, or Porte des Lions (until 17:15).
activities.notes: ✅ CONFIRMED - timed entry 19/10/2026 at 11:00, free with Museum Pass. Enter via Carrousel du Louvre, Pyramid, or Porte des Lions (until 17:15) entrance. World's largest art museum - CRITICAL: it's MASSIVE, you cannot see everything in a 3-hour session. Focus on must-sees: Mona Lisa, Venus de Milo, Winged Victory of Samothrace, plus 1-2 wings matching your interests (Ancient Egypt, Italian Renaissance, French painting, sculpture).

timeBlocks.name: lunch
timeBlocks.description: Quick lunch near the Louvre/Tuileries - keep it short, Sainte-Chapelle has a confirmed 15:30 slot.

activities.name: Lunch near Louvre
activities.notes: Options: Carrousel du Louvre food court (stays inside), café in Tuileries, or bistro on Rue Saint-Honoré. Keep it quick - Sainte-Chapelle entry is confirmed for 15:30, no flexibility on that time.

timeBlocks.name: afternoon
timeBlocks.description: Walk to Île de la Cité, visit La Conciergerie (same combined ticket, no reservation needed), then CONFIRMED Sainte-Chapelle entry at 15:30.

activities.name: Walk to Île de la Cité
activities.notes: 10 min walk from Louvre across Pont Neuf (oldest bridge in Paris) to Île de la Cité island.

activities.name: La Conciergerie
activities.notes: SAME COMBINED TICKET as Sainte-Chapelle - no separate reservation or extra cost, just walk in. Only Sainte-Chapelle has the fixed 15:30 timed slot, so visit the Conciergerie first while waiting. Former royal palace turned revolutionary prison, Marie Antoinette's cell, French Revolution history.

activities.name: Sainte-Chapelle
activities.timeRestriction: CONFIRMED timed entry 15:30 on 19/10/2026. Open 09:00-17:00 (Oct-Mar), last entry 40 min before close.
activities.notes: ✅ CONFIRMED - ticket #759304488215281, timed entry 19/10/2026 at 15:30 - this is a COMBINED TICKET that also covers La Conciergerie (same admission, no extra cost). STUNNING 13th-century Gothic chapel, 15 stained-glass windows floor-to-ceiling (15m high). On a sunny day the light through the glass is breathtaking - one of the most beautiful sights in Paris. PLEASE ARRIVE ON TIME - do not arrive before your slot, but don't be late either.

timeBlocks.budget: free (walk) - Sainte-Chapelle & Conciergerie included in Museum Pass

timeBlocks.name: late_afternoon
timeBlocks.description: Walk/metro to the Panthéon and visit with the Museum Pass in the FINAL slot before closing (last entry 17:15, closes 18:00 Oct-Mar) - this is the closest you can get to a 'golden hour' visit, since the Panthéon closes before literal sunset (~19:00) in October.

activities.name: Walk/Metro to Panthéon
activities.notes: 15-20 min walk from Île de la Cité to the Panthéon in the Latin Quarter, or a short metro ride.

activities.name: Panthéon (Interior - Museum Pass, last entry slot)
activities.timeRestriction: Open 10:00-18:00 (Oct-Mar). Last entry 17:15. BOOK TIMED ENTRY if possible for the last slot.
activities.notes: MUSEUM PASS INCLUDED - rated 8/10: cheap to climb and much less crowded late in the day, so you can actually enjoy it. Neoclassical mausoleum (saw the exterior Day 1, now go inside!). Crypt contains tombs of French heroes: Voltaire, Rousseau, Victor Hugo, Marie Curie, Alexandre Dumas, Émile Zola. Foucault's Pendulum demonstrates Earth's rotation. IMPORTANT: closes at 18:00 in October, well before actual sunset (~19:00) - this is the closest to a 'sunset visit' that's feasible; catch the real sunset afterward from outside or later at Montmartre.

bookingDetails.advanceTimeNeeded: Book the last entry slot (around 17:00-17:15) with the Museum Pass if online booking is available

timeBlocks.budget: free (walk) or €2.15 (metro) - Panthéon included in Museum Pass

timeBlocks.name: evening
timeBlocks.description: Walk from the Panthéon to Comptoir Coréen - Soju Bar (3rd arr., near Arts et Métiers) for dinner - it's within easy walking distance.

activities.name: Walk to Comptoir Coréen - Soju Bar
activities.notes: About 1.1 km / ~20 min walk from the Panthéon, heading north through the Latin Quarter and across the Seine toward the Arts et Métiers area (3rd arr.).

activities.name: Comptoir Coréen - Soju Bar Dinner
activities.notes: Best Korean food in Paris by far, according to local recommendation. Korean dishes + soju bar. Within walkable distance from the Panthéon, no need for RER/metro.

activities.name: Metro back to Hostel
activities.notes: Metro back toward the 19th arr., roughly 20-25 min.

alternatives.name: Palace of Versailles
alternatives.reason_not_selected: Removed per user request. Versailles required a half-day round trip outside Paris and wasn't worth the time cost vs. consolidating all Museum Pass attractions into Paris proper across 2 back-to-back days.

alternatives.name: Skip Conciergerie if tight on time
alternatives.reason_not_selected: Optional add-on since it's in the same complex as Sainte-Chapelle and the pass makes it free - but the Panthéon's last-entry slot in the late afternoon is the priority, so drop Conciergerie first if running behind.
alternatives.when_to_add: Keep as a flexible buffer activity

alternatives.name: Musée d'Orsay
alternatives.reason_not_selected: REMOVED - Day 3 falls on a Monday, and Musée d'Orsay is closed Mondays. User decided to skip Orsay entirely rather than restructure Day 2/3 further. Panthéon (Museum Pass included) now fills this slot instead, scheduled for the last entry before closing.
alternatives.when_to_add: Not applicable this trip - would need a different pass day that isn't a Monday

research_notes.notes: Day 3 is Museum Pass Day 2 (FINAL DAY - expires tonight). This day falls on a MONDAY, so Musée d'Orsay (closed Mondays) was dropped entirely per user decision. Panthéon was added instead in the last entry slot (16:30-18:00) using the Museum Pass - this is the closest to a 'sunset visit' that's feasible, since the Panthéon's Oct-Mar hours close at 18:00, before the actual sunset (~19:00). The 2-day Museum Pass covers: Hôtel de la Marine, Invalides, Arc de Triomphe (Day 2) + Louvre, Sainte-Chapelle, Conciergerie, Panthéon (Day 3) - seven attractions total. Evening dinner changed from Saint-Germain-des-Prés to Comptoir Coréen - Soju Bar (3rd arr., near Arts et Métiers) per user request - it's an easy ~20 min walk from the Panthéon, no RER/metro needed to get there.

days.title: Eiffel Tower, Galerie Lafayette & Rue Mouffetard

timeBlocks.name: early_morning
timeBlocks.description: Quick visit to the Eiffel Tower - just the 1st floor, for the anecdote (tower opens 09:30). Not covered by Museum Pass (pass already expired).

activities.name: Metro/RER to Eiffel Tower
activities.notes: Metro/RER combination from the 19th arr. to the 7th arr. (~35-40 min). Tower opens at 09:30 - no rush to arrive earlier.

activities.name: Eiffel Tower - 1st Floor (Quick Visit)
activities.timeRestriction: Opens 09:30. BOOK AHEAD - even the 1st floor ticket sells out.
activities.notes: A quick, cheaper visit just to go up and say you did it ('for the anecdote') - stairs ticket to the 1st floor only, skipping the full 2nd floor/summit experience. NOT covered by Museum Pass (pass has expired by Day 4 anyway). Check exact ticket tiers on the official site - stairs access typically includes the 1st floor en route to the 2nd.

bookingDetails.advanceTimeNeeded: Book a few days to a couple weeks ahead - 1st floor tickets have more availability than full summit tickets but can still sell out

activities.cost: ~€6-11 (student, 1st floor only - verify exact tier at booking)

timeBlocks.name: morning
timeBlocks.description: Transit to the Opera district for Galerie Lafayette's free rooftop terrace and famous stained-glass dome (Palais Garnier removed - closed during this visit).

activities.name: Transit to Opéra
activities.notes: Metro/RER, roughly 35-40 min from the Eiffel Tower area to Opéra.

activities.name: Galerie Lafayette Rooftop & Dome
activities.timeRestriction: Terrace typically open ~09:30-19:30, check seasonal hours, weather-dependent
activities.notes: Free rooftop terrace with panoramic views over Paris (Opéra, Sacré-Cœur, Eiffel Tower in the distance). Also worth going inside briefly to see the stunning stained-glass dome at the famous department store. Now the main Opera-district stop since Palais Garnier is closed during this visit (check if it reopens for a future trip).
activities.opening_hours: Check current terrace hours on arrival

timeBlocks.name: midday_transit
timeBlocks.description: Transit from the Opera district down to Rue Mouffetard in the 5th arr.

activities.name: Metro to Rue Mouffetard
activities.notes: Metro, roughly 25-30 min from Opéra to the Rue Mouffetard area.

timeBlocks.name: lunch
timeBlocks.description: Rue Mouffetard food exploration for lunch - lively market street with a bit of everything, including exotic/international food stalls.

activities.name: Rue Mouffetard Food Exploration & Lunch
activities.timeRestriction: Most stalls/restaurants open through lunch and early afternoon
activities.notes: Lively market street in the 5th arr. with a bit of everything, including many exotic/international food stalls - good spot to try Asian or Indian food. Good place to grab a quiche (€2.50-5), crêpe, or a charcuterie/cheese planche for lunch.

timeBlocks.name: afternoon
timeBlocks.description: Short walk from Rue Mouffetard to Île de la Cité, then free walk around the islands - Place Dauphine, Notre-Dame exterior, Pont Neuf. All free, no pass needed.

activities.name: Walk to Île de la Cité
activities.notes: Short ~15 min walk from Rue Mouffetard down to the islands, crossing near the Panthéon area (seen Day 3) - the two neighborhoods are right next to each other.

activities.name: Place Dauphine
activities.notes: Tranquil triangular square on western tip of Île de la Cité. Hidden gem - locals playing pétanque, quiet cafés.

activities.name: Cathédrale Notre-Dame
activities.timeRestriction: CHECK if interior reopened post-2019 fire. Exterior always accessible.
activities.notes: Gothic cathedral (1163-1345). Damaged in 2019 fire, restoration status should be checked closer to travel date. Exterior + square always viewable - flying buttresses, gargoyles, rose windows (if interior open). FREE entry if open.

activities.name: Pont Neuf & Seine Banks
activities.notes: Relaxed stroll along the Seine quays - bouquinistes (booksellers), views back toward Notre-Dame and the islands.

timeBlocks.name: evening
timeBlocks.description: Transit back toward the hostel neighborhood, relaxed Canal Saint-Martin evening with dinner - trendy area with bars, cafés, and the canal locks, just 5 min from the hostel.

activities.name: Metro back to Canal Saint-Martin
activities.notes: Metro, roughly 20-25 min from the islands back toward the Canal Saint-Martin / hostel area.

activities.name: Canal Saint-Martin Evening & Dinner
activities.timeRestriction: Bars/restaurants typically open through the evening
activities.notes: Trendy area with bars, cafés, and the canal locks, just 5 min from the hostel. A relaxed, low-key way to close out the trip's last full evening in Paris - no rush since everything is close to 'home'.

alternatives.name: Palais Garnier
alternatives.reason_not_selected: REMOVED - the opera house is closed during this visit (performance/rehearsal or maintenance closure). Galerie Lafayette's free rooftop terrace and dome next door now fills this slot instead.
alternatives.when_to_add: Check opening status for a future trip - worth revisiting if open

alternatives.name: Bourse de Commerce (Modern Art Museum)
alternatives.reason_not_selected: Pinault Collection contemporary art museum near Louvre. Would add another paid ticket to an already lighter day - only if modern art is a priority.
alternatives.when_to_add: Morning instead of the arcade walk

alternatives.name: Père-Lachaise Cemetery
alternatives.reason_not_selected: Far east 20th arr. Famous graves: Jim Morrison, Oscar Wilde, Chopin, Édith Piaf. Different vibe from the islands walk.
alternatives.when_to_add: Could replace the afternoon islands walk if you prefer cemetery over river strolling

alternatives.name: Saint-Étienne-du-Mont Church
alternatives.reason_not_selected: Next to the Panthéon (visited Day 3), FREE, 30 min. Beautiful rood screen, St Geneviève's tomb.
alternatives.when_to_add: Could add on Day 3 after Panthéon if you have 30 extra min, or walk by on the way to Rue Mouffetard

research_notes.notes: Day 4: Palais Garnier removed (closed during this visit) - Galerie Lafayette's free rooftop terrace/dome is now the main Opera-district stop, and the whole day shifted ~75 min earlier since there's less to do there. Eiffel Tower quick 1st-floor visit, Rue Mouffetard lunch, islands walk, and Canal Saint-Martin dinner remain unchanged in content, just re-timed earlier.

timeBlocks.name: early_morning
timeBlocks.description: Pack, check out, metro/transfer to Gare du Nord, board Eurostar to London. Pure logistics day - no activities.

activities.name: Check Out & Leave Hostel
activities.timeRestriction: Early departure - check out night before if possible
activities.notes: Wake ~05:45, final pack, check out (or store luggage and check out night before). Leave hostel 06:15 with all bags.

activities.name: Metro to Gare du Nord
activities.notes: Metro toward Gare du Nord (~10-15 min). Allow extra time for passport control and security - Eurostar recommends arriving ~45-60 min before departure.

activities.name: Eurostar to London St Pancras
activities.timeRestriction: Departure 07:32, arrives 09:00 (2h 28m). Passport control + security required before boarding.
activities.notes: ✅ CONFIRMED - Eurostar, Coach 4 - Seat 93, booking ref 2PX4VY. Departs Paris Gare du Nord 07:32, arrives London St Pancras Int'l 09:00. REMINDER: Complete Passenger Information (API) online and ensure you have your UK ETA before travel.

alternatives.name: Early Morning Montmartre Walk (04:00-06:00)
alternatives.reason_not_selected: Originally considered 4am wake-up for Montmartre sunrise before departure. REJECTED - too rushed, not enjoyable, misses the point of Montmartre experience. Moved Montmartre to Day 1 evening sunset instead - MUCH better!
alternatives.when_to_add: Don't. Already done Day 1 evening.

alternatives.name: Canal Saint-Martin Dawn Walk
alternatives.reason_not_selected: 5 min from hostel, could do 05:30-06:00 before leaving. But with luggage and early wake, not recommended. Canal is better enjoyed casually another time.
alternatives.when_to_add: Only if you wake early naturally and want quiet moment before departure

research_notes.notes: Day 5 is pure departure logistics. NO activities - just efficient transit to Gare du Nord for the confirmed 07:32 Eurostar to London. St Christopher's Inn location is close to the Line 5 metro corridor toward Gare du Nord. Budget: €2.15 metro only (Eurostar pre-booked). SIMPLE departure day - no stress!

must_try_dishes.description: Buttery, flaky pastry. Best fresh in morning from boulangerie.
Flaky pastry with chocolate bars inside. Morning staple.
Toasted sandwich with ham, Gruyère cheese, béchamel sauce. Add fried egg on top for croque-madame.
Classic Burgundy stew with beef, red wine, mushrooms, onions, carrots. Slow-cooked comfort food.
Chicken cooked in red wine with mushrooms, onions, bacon. Traditional bistro dish.
Grilled steak with crispy fries. Simple but quintessentially French. Order 'saignant' (rare) or 'à point' (medium).
Snails cooked in garlic-parsley butter. Classic French appetizer. Not for everyone but worth trying!
Caramelized onion soup topped with toasted bread and melted Gruyère cheese.
Rich custard dessert with caramelized sugar crust on top. Crack it with your spoon!
Apples caramelized in butter and sugar, baked with pastry on top, then flipped. Served warm with cream or ice cream.
Delicate almond meringue cookies with ganache filling. Not the coconut macaroon! Ladurée and Pierre Hermé are famous shops.
Not traditionally French but iconic in Le Marais Jewish quarter. L'As du Fallafel is world-famous. Chickpea fritters in pita with salad, tahini, fried eggplant.

Great French cheese tradition - any respectable bistro has a 'planche' with cheeses + cured meats. MUST TRY: Camembert, Roquefort, Brie. Recommended spot: Café des Beaux Arts (near the Louvre) - good prices, comfortable.
Cheese-based specialties - many restaurants specialize in ONLY fondue or raclette. Great cold-weather comfort food, usually shared.

One of the best quick options - savory tart with various fillings. Try Quiche Lorraine (ham & cheese), Bleu (blue cheese), or vegetable. Any boulangerie sells them; in the 5th arr. this is a great Rue Mouffetard snack.
Classic, cereal, or plain - available everywhere, cheap, reliable snack/meal base.
White beans with sausage, pork, and sometimes duck - originally from the south of France but a beloved Parisian bistro classic.
Duck slow-cooked in its own fat, served with potatoes. Rich, classic French comfort food.
Great as street food anywhere - especially good late at night (even at 3am from a street stand).
Recommended to buy from a supermarket as an easy comfort-food dessert to bring back to the hostel.

drinks_and_rituals.description: Standard coffee in France is espresso. Small, strong, black. Order at bar for cheaper price than sitting.
Espresso with steamed milk (similar to cappuccino). French typically only drink this at breakfast, never after lunch/dinner.
France is wine country! House wine (vin de la maison) is usually good quality and affordable. Order by glass (verre) or carafe.
French tradition of pre-dinner drinks. Kir (white wine + blackcurrant liqueur), pastis (anise spirit), or champagne. Often served with snacks (amuse-bouches).
Thick, rich hot chocolate (almost drinkable pudding). Parisian specialty, especially at Angelina near Tuileries.

restaurants.name: L'As du Fallafel
restaurants.notes: World-famous falafel. Long lines but worth it. CLOSED Friday evening & all Saturday. €8-12 per person.

restaurants.name: La Maison d'Isabelle
restaurants.notes: Recommended by Alan as 'best croissant in Paris'. Small bakery, arrive early.

restaurants.name: Rue Cler Market Street
restaurants.notes: Pedestrian market street with food shops, bakeries, cafés. Great for picnic supplies or casual lunch.

restaurants.name: Café de Flore
restaurants.typical_cost_per_person: 20-30 EUR (breakfast), more for a full meal
restaurants.notes: Historic literary café (Sartre, Hemingway frequented). Expensive but iconic. €20-30 for breakfast.

restaurants.name: Angelina Paris (Tuileries)
restaurants.notes: Famous for incredibly thick hot chocolate. Touristy but delicious. Long lines afternoon - go early or late.

restaurants.name: Café des Beaux Arts
restaurants.notes: Good prices and comfortable atmosphere, convenient near the Louvre. Great spot for a cheese/charcuterie board.

restaurants.name: Le Chalet du Parc
restaurants.notes: If you're in the 14th arr., this is the spot to try a proper Croque Monsieur/Madame.

restaurants.name: Bo&Mie
restaurants.notes: Good option for trying more elaborate/creative pastries beyond the basic croissant.

restaurants.name: Comptoir Coréen - Soju Bar
restaurants.notes: Best Korean food in Paris by far, according to local recommendation. Korean dishes + soju bar. Walkable distance from the Panthéon (~20 min) - no need for RER/metro.

special_meal_formats: Planche de charcuterie/fromage: cheese + cured meat board found at almost any proper bistro - great shared starter or light meal.
Rue Mouffetard (5th arr.) has a bit of everything, including many exotic/international food stalls - a great street to explore for Asian or Indian food in particular.
tourist_traps_to_avoid: Avoid restaurants with picture menus or aggressive touts on Champs-Élysées - overpriced and low quality
Skip the overpriced cafés directly facing Notre-Dame - walk one block away for 50% cheaper prices
Don't eat near major tourist sites (Eiffel Tower base, Louvre pyramid) - walk 5-10 min away for better value
Avoid eating dinner before 19:30 - you'll be marked as a tourist and service may be rushed
Skip branded macaron chains in train stations - go to actual Ladurée or Pierre Hermé boutiques, or local bakeries

average_food_budget_reference.note: Rough daily food budget guide for Paris (per person)
average_food_budget_reference.breakfast: 2-8 EUR (boulangerie pastry/coffee) up to 20-30 EUR (sit-down cafe like Café de Flore)
average_food_budget_reference.lunch: 8-15 EUR (falafel/market street food/bakery) up to 20-30 EUR (bistro)
average_food_budget_reference.dinner: 18-30 EUR (bistro classics like steak-frites or boeuf bourguignon)
average_food_budget_reference.snacks_and_drinks: 2-10 EUR (pastry, macaron, coffee, glass of wine)
average_food_budget_reference.daily_total_estimate: ~35-60 EUR/day eating casually/mid-range, more if doing iconic cafes (Café de Flore, Angelina) regularly

ticket_types.name: Navigo Easy Card
ticket_types.notes: Best for 2-4 days. Load t+ tickets (€2.15 each or €17.35 for 10). Shareable card.

ticket_types.name: Navigo Week Pass (Passe Navigo Semaine)
ticket_types.notes: BEST VALUE if arriving early in week (Mon-Wed). Unlimited metro, bus, RER, tram. Requires photo. Since you arrive Friday, might not be worth it.

ticket_types.name: Paris Visite Pass
ticket_types.notes: Tourist pass. Unlimited travel + some discounts. Zone 1-5 needed for Versailles. Compare with buying individual t+ tickets.

ticket_types.name: Single Ticket (t+)
ticket_types.validity: 90 min (transfers allowed on metro/RER within Paris, not on bus)
ticket_types.notes: Buy individually or carnet of 10 for €17.35 (€1.74 each). No need if you get week pass.

where_to_buy.metro_stations: Ticket windows or vending machines (accept card, some accept cash)
where_to_buy.FNAC_stores: Navigo cards, Paris Visite passes, Museum Pass
where_to_buy.online: RATP app for mobile tickets (not yet for all ticket types)

bike_rentals.name: Vélib' Métropole
bike_rentals.notes: Best option for Paris! 1,400+ stations. E-bikes available (green bikes, cost extra €1/30min). Highly recommended for Day 2 royal Paris route. Flat areas: Latin Quarter, Le Marais, Seine riverside. Avoid biking up Montmartre hill (use funicular or walk).

practical_tips: AVOID Châtelet station if possible - it has ~17 exits and is notoriously confusing to navigate. Use a less chaotic connecting station when there's a choice.

Many Paris metro lines split into two branches with different final destinations (e.g., Line 7, Line 13) - ALWAYS read the platform screen/train headsign carefully to confirm which branch you're boarding, not just the line number.
RER is faster than the metro for longer distances (fewer stops) but gets very crowded during peak hours (~10:00 and ~18:00) - avoid RER at these times if you can use metro instead.
Uber in Paris is relatively inexpensive and the fleet is almost entirely Tesla - a comfortable backup option for late nights or heavy luggage days.
Metro is fastest but can be crowded during rush hours (08:00-09:30, 17:30-19:30). Consider biking during these times.
Keep metro tickets until you exit - inspectors check and fine €50 for no ticket.
Pickpockets active on Line 1 (Louvre-Champs-Élysées) and Line 4 (Gare du Nord-Montparnasse). Keep valuables secure.
Many museums closed Mondays or Tuesdays - check before going. Louvre closed Tuesdays, Orsay closed Mondays (this is why Orsay was dropped from this itinerary - Day 3 falls on a Monday).
Student ID (ISIC card or university ID) gets discounts at most museums (30-50% off).
Free museum entry for EU students under 26 at many national museums (Louvre, Orsay, etc.). Check each museum's policy.
Tap water (l'eau du robinet) is free at restaurants - don't pay for bottled water unless you want it.
Tipping not required (service included) but rounding up or leaving €1-2 for good service is appreciated.
Learn basic phrases: 'Bonjour' (hello), 'Merci' (thank you), 'Pardon' (excuse me), 'L'addition, s'il vous plaît' (the bill, please).

full_trip_overview.description: Overview of all major stops across 5 days in Paris - from hostel through Latin Quarter, Montmartre, Le Marais, Royal Paris, Versailles, and back.

alternatives_considered.name: Hôtel Madrigal (original accommodation)
alternatives_considered.reason_not_selected: Switched to St Christopher's Inn - closer to Bercy bus station (15 min vs 25 min), near Canal/Montmartre, social hostel atmosphere, cheaper. Better for Bruges departure and social vibe.
alternatives_considered.notes: St Christopher's location in 19th saves 10 min on Day 5 departure and puts you near Montmartre (15 min metro).

alternatives_considered.name: 4-Day Museum Pass (€62)
alternatives_considered.reason_not_selected: 2-Day Museum Pass (€55) is more efficient. Concentrated museum days on Sat-Sun (Days 2-3). Day 1 is arrival/free sites, Day 4 is Louvre + individual tickets, Day 5 is departure. Saves €30 vs trying to use 4-day pass with gaps.
alternatives_considered.notes: 2-day pass strategy covers: Hôtel de la Marine, Invalides, Arc de Triomphe (Day 2), Versailles, Orsay (Day 3). Louvre separate ticket Day 4 (€17 student).

alternatives_considered.name: Day 5 Early Morning Montmartre (04:00-06:00)
alternatives_considered.reason_not_selected: Too rushed before 06:30 FlixBus. Moved Montmartre to Day 1 late afternoon/evening for sunset at Sacré-Cœur - much better experience and no 4am wake-up!
alternatives_considered.notes: Day 5 now pure departure logistics (05:45 leave hostel → 06:00 at bus station).

alternatives_considered.name: Le Marais on Day 4 (original plan)
alternatives_considered.reason_not_selected: Moved Le Marais to Day 1 evening to free up Day 4 for Palais Garnier + Louvre + Islands (all central 1st arr.). Le Marais fits better on Day 1 - arrival day with energy for social neighborhood evening.
alternatives_considered.notes: Day 4 now: Palais Garnier → Louvre (WIP list) → Île de la Cité (Sainte-Chapelle, Notre-Dame) → Panthéon interior.

alternatives_considered.name: Père-Lachaise Cemetery
alternatives_considered.reason_not_selected: Far east (20th arr.), 90 min visit, doesn't fit Day 4 flow. Can swap with Panthéon if you prefer cemetery (Jim Morrison, Oscar Wilde, Chopin graves) over crypt (Voltaire, Rousseau, Hugo, Curie).
alternatives_considered.notes: Optional alternative to Panthéon on Day 4 evening. Metro Line 2/3 to Père Lachaise station.

alternatives_considered.name: Before Sunset Film Locations (Le Pure Café, Cour de l'Étoile-d'Or)
alternatives_considered.reason_not_selected: Niche interest, not core Paris sites. Can add to Day 1 or Day 4 Le Marais time if you're a film fan.
alternatives_considered.notes: Le Pure Café is in 11th arr. near Bastille - 15 min walk from Place des Vosges.

research_notes.notes: Paris itinerary optimized for 4.5 days (arrive Fri 10:35, depart Mon 06:30). Strategy: 2-Day Museum Pass for Sat-Sun to hit Versailles + major monuments, separate Louvre ticket on Mon to avoid Sunday crowds and maximize time. Student discounts throughout (€14.50 Eiffel stairs, €17 Louvre, €11.50 Sainte-Chapelle, €11.50 Panthéon, €12 Palais Garnier). Total museum/monument costs ~€165-185. Accommodation change to St Christopher's Inn saves time for Bruges departure and provides social hostel experience + proximity to Montmartre/Canal Saint-Martin. Bike-friendly days: 1 (Latin Quarter), 2 (Royal Paris), 4 (Le Marais). Skip bikes for: Day 3 (Versailles RER), Day 5 (departure), Montmartre uphill (funicular or walk). Louvre viewing list set as WIP - to be added later based on specific interests.
